intro: The SC10 deliberately has no weight sensor, so weight-related advice for other boxes does not apply. It relies on six infrared sensors instead, which brings its own small set of quirks, and it has firm size requirements for the cats using it.

facts.text: No weight sensor: cats are detected by six infrared sensors, so floor levelling does not affect it.
Cats must weigh more than 3 lb and stand at least 5.91 in tall to be detected.
Never fully closes, leaving a permanent exit route.
A 12 L waste drawer and 6 L litter capacity, rated for about 10 days with one adult cat.

symptoms.title: A cat is not detected
symptoms.summary: A cat uses the box without the unit registering it.
causes: Meowant specifies cats over 3 lb and at least 5.91 in tall; smaller cats fall below what the sensors detect.

fixes.detail: Confirm the cat meets both thresholds. Kittens should use a conventional tray until they do.

symptoms.escalate: If a cat well above both thresholds is missed, contact Meowant.

symptoms.title: There is no weight data in the app
symptoms.summary: The app shows visits and frequency but no weights.
causes: The SC10 has no weight sensor by design.

fixes.detail: Use frequency and timing trends instead. This is how the SC10 is built, not a fault.

symptoms.escalate: If you need weight tracking, the SC10 is the wrong box for you rather than a broken one.

symptoms.title: Cleaning keeps stopping with no cat present
symptoms.summary: Cycles interrupt as if a cat had entered.
causes: An object, wall or curtain within the sensor field.

fixes.detail: Wipe the infrared sensors with a dry cloth.
Move the unit away from walls and curtains and remove nearby objects.

symptoms.escalate: Persistent false triggers on clean sensors with clear surroundings suggest a sensor fault for Meowant support.
